defects.description: Product output stream rewritten to work around a pyte (test emulator) mis-parse of CSI > Pp m. It is well documented and inert on XTMODKEYS-aware terminals, but it is permanent product code that exists for the acceptance emulator. It relies on the claim that the renderer pen is plain when Bubble Tea emits XTMODKEYS; if a future Bubble Tea emitted it mid-frame, the inserted CSI m would silently drop styling. A sequence split across Write calls would also miss its reset (acknowledged by the implementer). Neither was observed.

On a short write the returned byte count maps bytes of the expanded buffer q to bytes of p (clamped to len(p)), so n is not an accurate offset into p. An error is always returned and Bubble Tea ignores n, so there is no practical effect.

Matching and SGR insertion work on runes, not grapheme clusters. A filter that matches a base letter of a decomposed sequence (e + U+0301) or a ZWJ emoji part would put SGR 4/24 inside a cluster. Outside the spec's ASCII/CJK test scope; this is inferred from reading the code and was not observed.
The pty test drives keys with fixed 250 ms sleeps and an 8 s timeout. Timing-based, so it may flake under heavy load (not observed).
The comment 'filter mode survives an open/close cycle' is inaccurate: help can only open outside filter mode, and the step only checks that the render is unchanged.

notes: Case folding: T3 requires the existing filter rule. matchSpan uses strings.ToLower like profile.Filter, which is a 1:1 rune mapping (unicode.ToLower), so rune indexes align with Sanitize output. Rune-wise substring match equals strings.Contains on valid UTF-8. ASCII-only folding is a T2 concern and not applicable here.
ansi.Truncate (x/ansi v0.11.8) keeps escape sequences after the cut, so a clipped match does not leave underline on. TestMatchHighlightTruncated covers this.

Bubble Tea v2.0.10 detects the output terminal through the term.File interface (tty_unix.go:30, tty_windows.go:36), which the wrapper satisfies via Fd/Read/Write/Close. Windows was not run (compile/vet only per the implementer).
Part C refilter correctly handles an empty prior result (prev=-1 -> row 0). Stateless scrolling keeps the selected row visible with a full window, which matches the K17 part C predicate.

Help overlay: Ctrl-C is checked before the help gate. WindowSizeMsg/InterruptMsg/TermMsg/HangupMsg are handled regardless. Esc/? close it without touching filter state. In filter mode, ? falls through to the printable append.
Security: displayed text stays Sanitize'd. Only fixed SGR constants are inserted. The filter is printable-checked. The output regex is linear. No secrets are involved.
